summary: The first statement of how the Network Working Group's notes should work. Anyone at any site could write a note, and notes were meant to be timely rather than polished, covering host software and other aspects of the network. This informal approach is the origin of the Request for Comments series. It was replaced by RFC 10.

eli5.summary: This note sets the club rules for sharing ideas: anyone can write one, and a rough idea shared fast is better than a perfect one shared late.

questions: how did the rfc series start
what are network working group notes

subtitle: The original ground rules for sharing ideas quickly over the network

tldr.problem: The Network Working Group needed a way to share timely ideas about network software and HOST systems without waiting for polished, formal documentation.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3 establishes that anyone can write and submit notes, with the explicit goal that rough ideas shared quickly are better than perfect ones shared late.
tldr.outcome: This informal approach became the foundation for the Request for Comments series, which continues to guide internet standards today.

today: RFC 3 is obsoleted by RFC 10, but the principle it established—that timely sharing of rough ideas is valuable—became the enduring foundation of the entire RFC series and internet standards process.

sections.title: The Network Working Group
sections.content: RFC 3 defines how the Network Working Group (NWG) will communicate. The group consists of researchers from UCLA, Stanford Research Institute and other sites concerned with HOST software and network strategies. Unlike traditional technical documentation, anyone at any site could write a note and submit it to the series, and notes were encouraged to be timely rather than polished.
sections.eli5: A group of researchers needed to share ideas fast. The rule was simple: write your idea down, even if it is rough, and send it in.

sections.title: Content and Style
sections.content: Notes can cover any thought, suggestion or experiment related to HOST software or the network itself. Philosophical positions without examples, specific implementation techniques without background, and questions without answers are all acceptable. The minimum length for a note is a single sentence. This explicit permission to be informal and incomplete was intentional, designed to ease the natural hesitation to publish something unpolished.
sections.eli5: You can write about any network idea, even if it is not finished or polished. Even one sentence is enough to share.

sections.title: Format and Distribution
sections.content: Every NWG note should carry standard information: the header 'Network Working Group' with a serial number (assigned by Bill Duvall at SRI), the author and affiliation, the date, and a title (which does not need to be unique). One copy is sent to designated recipients at research institutions. The note establishes that others may reproduce the document locally if needed.
sections.eli5: Each note gets a number and header so people know where it came from. One copy is distributed to key sites, and anyone can copy it after that.
